questions.q: What is Azure Resource Manager (ARM), in relation to the tools used earlier in this course?
options: Azure's control plane — every resource created by PowerShell, Python, or the CLI in this course ultimately goes through it
A competing cloud provider to Azure
A Python library with no connection to the Azure CLI
A feature that only exists inside Bicep, not Azure itself
questions.explain: ARM sits underneath every resource-creation path in Azure, whether it's a PowerShell cmdlet, a Python SDK call, or an az CLI command.

questions.q: What is an ARM template, and what format is it written in?
options: Azure's native deployment format, written in JSON and submitted directly to Azure Resource Manager
A YAML file that only works with AWS CloudFormation
A compiled binary with no human-readable form
A PowerShell script with a .arm file extension
questions.explain: ARM templates are ARM's native JSON format for declaring resources — readable, but verbose compared to Bicep.

questions.q: What does Bicep actually produce when you run a deployment?
options: Bicep compiles down to ARM JSON, which is what Azure Resource Manager actually receives and processes
Bicep deploys directly to AWS, bypassing Azure Resource Manager entirely
Bicep produces a PowerShell script that then runs the deployment
Bicep has no relationship to ARM templates at all
questions.explain: Bicep is a DSL whose entire purpose is to compile to ARM JSON, via az bicep build or automatically during deployment.

questions.q: Which Azure CLI command deploys a Bicep file to a resource group?
options: az deployment group create --resource-group <rg> --template-file <file>.bicep
az bicep run <file>.bicep
New-AzStorageAccount -BicepFile <file>.bicep
az cloudformation deploy --template-file <file>.bicep
questions.explain: az deployment group create, pointed at a .bicep file, is the standard way to deploy — the same CLI already used for imperative commands in Chapter 4.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does Microsoft now recommend Bicep over hand-written ARM JSON?
options: Bicep is shorter to write and comes with real tooling like VS Code IntelliSense and Portal-based export, while still compiling to the same full-featured ARM JSON
ARM JSON has been fully discontinued and no longer works
Bicep can deploy to AWS and Azure interchangeably
Bicep requires no Azure subscription to use
questions.explain: Bicep offers cleaner syntax and strong tooling without sacrificing any ARM capability — parameters, loops, and outputs all carry over.
